title: Check if bit 1 is set. flags = 0x06. What does this print?
explain: == is stronger than &. So it runs as flags & (MASK == MASK), which is flags & 1 = 0. The test fails, although bit 1 is set. Always write (flags & MASK) == MASK. Same trap as in register checks.

title: On the Uno, micros() is a 32-bit unsigned long in microseconds. When does it wrap to 0?
explain: 2^32 µs = 4294.97 s = 71.6 minutes. millis() wraps after 49.7 days, but micros() is 1000 times faster. The fix is the same as in lesson 6: use unsigned subtraction, now - start >= timeout.

title: Uno ADC clock = 16 MHz / 128. One conversion takes 13 ADC clocks. How long is one analogRead()?
explain: ADC clock = 125 kHz, so 13 / 125000 = 104 µs. That is about 9600 readings per second at most. Reading the TMP36 in a fast loop gives the same value many times. Averaging 8 readings costs less than 1 ms.

title: A 7805 needs about 2 V of dropout. You feed it 6 V from 4 AA batteries. What is the output?
options: About 4 V, it follows the input
explain: A 7805 needs Vin of about 7 V or more to give a stable 5 V. With 6 V in, the output drops to about 4 V and changes with the load. A 9 V battery is fine. For a low input, use a low-dropout (LDO) regulator.

title: A blue LED has Vf = 3.0 V. It is on a 3.3 V pin with a 220 Ω resistor. What is the LED current?
explain: I = (3.3 - 3.0) / 220 = 1.4 mA. The LED is very dim. Vf changes with the LED and temperature, so some LEDs may not light at all. With a small voltage margin, use a lower resistor or a higher supply.

title: LED is on all the time, even with no button press. Tap the bug.
explain: The ; after the if is an empty statement. The block below always runs. The compiler may not warn. Always put the { on the same line as if, or turn on -Wempty-body.

title: Reject invalid pin in GPIO_Init

pr.author: junior-dev
pr.title: Reject invalid pin in GPIO_Init
pr.body: Added a check. A bad pin now returns -1.

explain: The check comes after the register writes. With pin 20 the shift is 40 on a 32-bit value (undefined), and a wrong register bit may change first. Validate all arguments before the first write. Also check mode <= 3.

title: Before you place a capacitor: 4 checks
bullets: Polarity: an electrolytic has a stripe on the minus side. Reversed, it can heat up and burst.
Voltage rating: use at least 1.5 to 2 times the real voltage. A 6.3 V cap on a 5 V rail is too close.
Ceramic (100 nF) next to each chip power pin: it fixes fast spikes. Electrolytic (10 µF and up) near the regulator: it holds slow changes.
Short wires. A long wire adds inductance, and the cap helps much less.

title: STM32F4 PUPDR: 2 bits per pin, 01 = pull-up, 10 = pull-down. You set pull-up for pin 3. What is printed?
explain: Pin 3 uses bits 7:6, so the shift is 3 * 2 = 6. 1u << 6 = 64. A pull-down (10) would be 2u << 6 = 128. As with MODER, clear the 2 bits first with &= ~(3u << 6) before you OR the new value.

title: analogWrite(LED, 128) gives 50% duty. How does the LED look to your eye?
explain: Average current is half, but the eye sees brightness on a curve (about gamma 2.2). 50% duty looks like about 70% bright. For smooth fades, use a gamma table. 490 Hz is too fast to see.
